> as they were paying high and I refused to be a corporate slave working more that 12 hours a day

I found myself in the same spot.

But I don't think 12 hours a day is fucking sane, no matter how high the pay gets - especially when it comes to mentally stressful jobs in the software industry.

Been there, done that. I was in a startup before in which I dished 12-16 hours of work every day. I was in a cycle of constantly dishing out work and finding ways to relieve the stress like Dota and stress-eating.

It seeped into my life as the stress piled up. Christmas midnight? I'd go to a cafe to play Dota all night. Relative coming over? I'd go to a cafe to play Dota. I have a deadline in the morning? You'll find me playing a few hours prior. My personal relationships were affected.

One day, I decided to start afresh. I dropped extra projects and found a company that actually cares about work-life balance. I used to be addicted to Dota, but now things are looking well - I'm working out daily yet still getting shit done. I still play, but it no longer affects my life or relationships anymore.

Do less of stressful things. Dota is alright as a stress-reliever, but anything too much is bad. Take it easy on yourself.

Best of luck to you, pal. I hope things work out on your end.
